literal: If one speaks of the measure of the greatness of those who have renounced, it is like counting all those who have died in the world.
translation: To measure the greatness of those who have renounced all desires is like trying to count all the people who have ever died on this earth.
modern: ஆசைகளைத் துறந்தவர்களுடைய பெருமையின் எல்லையைச் சொல்ல முயல்வது, இவ்வுலகத்தில் இதுவரை பிறந்து இறந்தவர்களை எண்ணிக் கணக்கிடுவதைப் போன்றது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the infinite nature of the greatness of sages who have renounced worldly desires. The author uses a striking, impossible task as a comparison: counting every single person who has ever died on earth since the beginning of time. Just as it is impossible to keep a tally of all the deceased throughout human history, it is equally impossible to define or limit the spiritual stature of those who have conquered their desires. The key words 'துறந்தார்' (those who renounced) and 'பெருமை' (greatness) establish the subject, while 'இறந்தாரை எண்ணிக்கொண்டற்று' (like counting the dead) provides the vivid, hyperbolic analogy that emphasizes the boundless nature of their virtue.
